email.body1:
Paul, saw Ridgeline ship Intelligent Operations and Market Intelligence, with new AI agents and clients like Driehaus and Winslow coming on.

When the platform story expands that fast, the list of investment firms worth a services conversation grows faster than any seller can personally work, and good accounts slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new hires: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Ridgeline off your product and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Paul, quick follow-up for Ridgeline.

With new products and logos landing, services demand is climbing, but most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number. The gap shows up late, and then the quarter is a scramble to recover.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Ridgeline's services team needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Paul, last bit of proof for Ridgeline.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Ridgeline's reply rate likely compares to other fintech platforms. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Paul, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling services pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Launching two new products is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a services-sales motion? I will tailor it to Ridgeline either way.
